facts.statement: Sarahsaurus was first described by Timothy B. Rowe, Hans-Dieter Sues, and Robert R. Reisz in 2011.
facts.quote: Sarahsaurus was first described by Timothy B. Rowe, Hans-Dieter Sues and Robert R. Reisz in 2011; the type species is Sarahsaurus aurifontanalis.

facts.statement: The genus name Sarahsaurus honors Sarah (Mrs. Ernest) Butler, an Austin philanthropist who funded the 'Dino Pit' exhibit.
facts.quote: The generic name honours Sarah (Mrs. Ernest) Butler, an Austin philanthropist.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Sarahsaurus were collected from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation near Gold Spring, Arizona.
facts.quote: All specimens of Sarahsaurus were collected from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation near Gold Spring, Arizona.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus is the fourth basal sauropodomorph dinosaur officially identified in North America.
facts.quote: Sarahsaurus is the fourth basal sauropodomorph dinosaur to have been officially identified in North America

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus possessed very large, powerful hands, which suggests it may have been an omnivore.
facts.quote: The animal is notable for possessing very large, powerful hands, possibly suggesting that it was an omnivore.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus was mid-sized for a basal sauropodomorph, with a vertebral column measuring more than 3.1 meters in length.
facts.quote: Sarahsaurus was mid-sized for a basal sauropodomorph, with its vertebral column measuring more than 3.1 m in length.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory Paul estimated Sarahsaurus to be 4 meters long and weigh 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Gregory Paul, in a 2016 popular book, estimated its length at 4 m and its body weight at 200 kg.

facts.statement: Each side of Sarahsaurus's upper jaw contained 20 teeth, with four in the premaxilla and sixteen in the maxilla.
facts.quote: Each side of the upper jaw was lined with 20 teeth – four in the premaxilla, the front bone of the upper jaw, and 16 in the maxilla which followed behind.

facts.statement: The teeth of Sarahsaurus had serrated cutting edges with up to 20 denticles per tooth.
facts.quote: Their cutting edges were serrated with up to 20 denticles per tooth.

facts.statement: There is no evidence that Sarahsaurus possessed a beak.
facts.quote: There is no evidence for a beak.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus's spine consisted of approximately 10 neck vertebrae, 14 trunk vertebrae, three hip vertebrae, and about 50 tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The spine comprised 10 cervical (neck) vertebrae; 14 dorsal (trunk) vertebrae; three sacral (hip) vertebrae; and ca. 50 caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade (scapula) of Sarahsaurus was hourglass-shaped.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) was hourglass-shaped.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus's humerus was more than half the length of its femur and featured a large, S-shaped deltopectoral crest extending for half the bone's length.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) was more than half the length of the femur (upper thigh bone), and had a large crest on its front side for muscle attachment, the deltopectoral crest, which extended for half the length of the bone and had an S-shaped edge.

facts.statement: The claw bone of the first finger in Sarahsaurus's hand was the largest.
facts.quote: In the hand, the ungual (claw bone) of the first finger was the largest.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus's tibia reached 84% of the length of its femur.
facts.quote: The tibia (shin bone) reached 84% of the length of the femur.

facts.statement: A 2018 cladistic analysis recovered Sarahsaurus and Ignavusaurus as massospondylids, supporting the original assignment of Sarahsaurus to the genus Massospondylus.
facts.quote: A 2018 cladistic analysis by Chapelle and Choiniere recovered Sarahsaurus and Ignavusaurus as massospondylids, mirroring the original assignment of Sarahsaurus to Massospondylus.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus lived approximately 199 to 182 million years ago during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: It has been surmised that the Kayenta Formation was deposited during the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic period, approximately 199 to 182 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sarahsaurus have been found in the Kayenta Formation, which spans northern Arizona, southeastern Utah, western Colorado, and northwestern New Mexico.
facts.quote: The Kayenta Formation is part of the Glen Canyon Group that includes formations not only in northern Arizona but also parts of southeastern Utah, western Colorado, and northwestern New Mexico.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus lived in an environment with a seasonal climate featuring abundant water in streams, ponds, and lakes.
facts.quote: The animals here were adapted to a seasonal climate and abundant water could be found in streams, ponds and lakes.

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Massospondylidae

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Sarahsaurus is Sarahsaurus aurifontanalis.
facts.quote: Type species: Sarahsaurus aurifontanalis

facts.statement: The genus Sarahsaurus was described by Rowe and colleagues in 2011.
facts.quote: Rowe et al. 2011

facts.statement: Sarahsaurus coexisted with theropods like Dilophosaurus and Kayentavenator, as well as armored dinosaurs such as Scelidosaurus and Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: Sarahsaurus shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as several theropods including Dilophosaurus, Kayentavenator, Coelophysis kayentakatae, and the "Shake N Bake" theropod, and the armored dinosaurs Scelidosaurus and Scutellosaurus.

facts.statement: The ecosystem of Sarahsaurus included diverse vertebrates such as hybodont sharks, lungfish, the frog Prosalirus, the turtle Kayentachelys, and the pterosaur Rhamphinion.
facts.quote: Vertebrates present in the Kayenta Formation at the time of Sarahsaurus included hybodont sharks, indeterminate bony fish, lungfish, salamanders, the frog Prosalirus, the caecilian Eocaecilia, the turtle Kayentachelys, a sphenodontian reptile, various lizards, and the pterosaur Rhamphinion.

facts.statement: Early crocodylomorphs like Calsoyasuchus and Protosuchus lived alongside Sarahsaurus in the Kayenta Formation.
facts.quote: Several early crocodylomorphs were present including Calsoyasuchus, Eopneumatosuchus, Kayentasuchus, and Protosuchus.

facts.statement: Coprolites and fossil tracks found in the area provide evidence of the presence of therapsids, lizard-like animals, and dinosaurs alongside Sarahsaurus.
facts.quote: Vertebrate trace fossils from this area included coprolites and the tracks of therapsids, lizard-like animals, and dinosaurs, which provided evidence that these animals were also present.

facts.statement: By the Middle Jurassic, the environment where Sarahsaurus lived was being encroached upon by a sandy dune field that later formed the Navajo Sandstone.
facts.quote: By the Middle Jurassic period it was being encroached upon from the north by a sandy dune field that would become the Navajo Sandstone.
